methodology: Median warm time per entry after symmetric 1.5×IQR outlier filtering; raw samples and exclusions are retained. Each runtime warms for at least 150 ms, calibrates a batch, then measures the recorded number of batches. Every timed return-value checksum is verified. Printed output is verified before timing; timed output uses a null sink (native) or byte callback (web). Formatting and runtime-specific I/O remain included. Includes the host call boundary and budget reset where required; excludes loading, process startup, downloads and offline compilation. Tiny examples emphasize call overhead. Host gate: every measured job runs pinned (inherited affinity, no wrapper) to one logical CPU of the quietest core, chosen again before each attempt once its other hyperthread has settled, and is repeated unless that CPU kept its clock within 3% of the job median (10th to 90th percentile), the median reached 95% of the clock calibrated at start, and the hyperthread sibling was busy at most 15% of the job; Go runs with GOMAXPROCS=1 on that CPU. Rejected attempts are retained with their observations.
